text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: inference-proxy-high-p95 -> pd:PD12345 links/docs: <https://pagerduty.local/incidents/PD12345>
incident-bot: Summary: p95 latency > 800ms across region-us-east-1 for 3m, auto-escalation schedule applied. Alert rule: infra.proxy.latency.p95 > 800ms (3m)
sara: ack @incident-bot @pagerduty-bot  :wave: I'm on it — pulling dashboards
sara: checks: logs, proxy pods, and canaries. first glance: routing looks normal, tails of CPU are fine
sara: ran: `kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=inference-proxy -o wide` -> all pods Ready=1/1
sara: logs show repeated latency spikes from a subset of requests hitting /v1/generate with long backend times. snippet:```[2026-03-15T08:14:12Z] req_id=6a3f service=proxy path=/v1/generate backend_ms=920 model=vicuna-13b user_tier=prod```
sara: but traffic volume steady — no sudden qps jump. tagging @mike for canary insight :eyes:
mike: looking now — checking synthetic canaries and schedule
mike: canary job runner shows a burst around 08:12-08:16 — multiple canaries overlapped due to a cron drift after deploy last night
mike: canary logs:```2026-03-15T08:12:05Z canary-id=cf-21 start
2026-03-15T08:12:07Z canary-id=cf-22 start
2026-03-15T08:12:10Z canary-id=cf-23 start```
mike: that explains small hot-spot on the proxy — they are small spikes but repeated, causing alert flapping. not seen in customer-facing traffic sampling
incident-bot: PagerDuty update: alert escalated to L2 (mike) due to repeated firing
sara: quick customer impact check: sampled production traffic traces for 08:10-08:20 -> error rate 0.0%, tail latency elevated for small percentage (~0.9% of requests) mostly synthetic user-agent `canary/1.0`. conclusion: no customer impact. marking as no-impact for now :white_check_mark:
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty note: Alert auto-resolved at 08:18 after 6m of recovery. (auto-resolve)
sara: thanks — looks like transient synthetic canary overlap. I’ll silence PD rule for the canary UA while we fix canary scheduling :thumbsup:
mike: creating temporary suppression rule for alert -> `suppress where user_agent contains "canary/" for 30m` (ops will harden later)
lina: noted — adding jitter to canary cron and bumping max-concurrency to avoid overlap. will open a follow-up PR: `infr/canary/schedule: add jitter`
ops-bot: Silence applied by mike on rule infra.proxy.latency.p95 for 30m (id: silence-9987)
sara: handoff: I'm going offline for a meeting in 20m — @mike can you own post-incident follow-up? I'll file the quick blameless note.
mike: got it. I'll add a short timeline and action items to the incident tracker. Quick note for postmortem: - root cause: canary runner concurrency/schedule drift - immediate mitigation: PD silence + jitter + max-concurrency - long-term: detect synthetic UA traffic and exclude from p95 alerting + add better canary scheduling sanity checks
sara: everyone, thumbs up if you agree with no customer impact and post-ops plan :+1:
lina: +1, will draft PR today
incident-bot: Follow-up: created incident ticket T-6789 for scheduling fix, assigned to lina, due 3 days.
mike: will also add an alert tag `suppressible:synthetic` to make future noisy canaries easier to filter
sara: closing thread here — will keep the silence until PR merges, and will kick off a short retro next week. thanks all for quick triage :clap:
pagerduty-bot: Incident PD12345 closed (auto-resolve). No acknowledged escalations to customer contacts.
